title: Life in the solar and father's grocery business
summary: Description of the two-room home, the move across the street, and his father's prosperous import, grocery and street-vendor business.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. Macho, at that time when you were five years old, Were you living in the solar?
Yes
Okay, describe to me your home and
how many children were living there with you and your mother.
Well by that time we were two. The rest - they - we moved across the street.
So you and Anisa were born in the solar. Right? And how many rooms did you have in el solar?
We had two.
Two rooms.
Two rooms; one for my father - one for Alicia and myself.
So how long do you remember living in el solar before you moved across the street?
Well, I was maybe about nine or ten. And then my father start the business that was, that made him made him very rich.
What business was that?
They were selling groceries.
Tell me about that.

Oh, that was very complicated thing for people. In those days like all these countries they have representation of merchandise: automobiles or whatever, electrical appliances. There were - so we didn't manufacture anything in Cuba, we was buying everything from the United States and from Spain; and from Europe a few things; and from China, the silk. All those stores they was owned by chinamen. They brought all those merchandise from China. - So my father have a lot of trucks or whatever and he used to transport from the - from the docks to the - to the business.
To the business site eh?
Yes, all the merchandise. We . . . .
So he was selling silks and what else?
And groceries
And groceries - For instance give me some examples. What kind of groceries?
Well, the groceries was rice, beans, lard, pork, you know, eh - what you call it - bacon, ham, that was coming from the United States - from Armour and Swift.
He had a street - - He was a street vendor?
Yes - - Yeah, he had a lot of vendors in the street.
Oh, he had people working for him too.
Working for him
